Importantly, the study also showed a reduction in the abundance of the potentially pathogenic Vibrionaceae family following the incorporation of poultry by-product protein hydrolysate, indicating potential health benefits for the shrimp. Overall, the results suggest that poultry by-product protein hydrolysate not only influences enzymatic activity positively but also beneficially modulates the gut microbiota. This study investigated the effects of extract from swiftlet nest (Collocalia fuciphago) on blood glucose levels and circulating endothelial cells (CEC) in rats (Rattus norvegicus) with induced hyperglycemia. Although several detection methods exist, many require extensive sample preparation prior to analysis, limiting their practical application. This study focused on developing a biosensor using an aptamer-DNAzyme conjugate aimed at label-free detection of melamine directly in raw milk without any sample preparation.
